skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray for signs of situs inversus or Kartagener's syndrome.
steps: Identify the side of the cardiac apex to determine heart position (levocardia vs. dextrocardia).
Locate the gastric air bubble and liver shadow to determine abdominal organ arrangement.
Confirm situs inversus if the heart is on the right (dextrocardia) AND the gastric bubble/liver are on the left (mirror image of normal).

skills.trigger: When distinguishing between primary ciliary dyskinesia manifestations (Kartagener's) and other causes of bronchiectasis or consolidation.
steps: Check for the specific triad components: situs inversus, chronic sinusitis (often not visible on CXR), and bronchiectasis.
Differentiate 'situs inversus' (complete mirror image: right heart + left stomach) from isolated 'dextrocardia' (right heart only) or normal anatomy.

Select the option describing the anatomical reversal (e.g., left-sided liver/right-sided heart) as the supporting finding for Kartagener's over options describing only lung parenchymal disease without mentioning the positional anomaly.
